recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any cleanup of non-rendered legacy comments, CapabilityStatement narrative branches, or retired unknown-content terminology artifacts should be handled under a separate issue rather than FHIR-18363.
issue_request: FHIR-18363 asked to remove the extensibility-page requirement that systems not accepting unknown extensions declare that in CapabilityStatement resources, because the CapabilityStatement.acceptUnknown mechanism had been removed.
initial_application: FHIR-14647/GF#14647 was applied in f0ec862a5f986e3a82bb9ef1a4fa32619c65d6e1 by removing/disabling CapabilityStatement.acceptUnknown. FHIR-18363 was then applied in cd5231d416ef0145942d6a04f15d50d66640be98, which removed the exact declaration bullet from source/extensibility.html.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini maps the extension type page to source/extensibility.html, and the current exchange guidance in that file omits the obsolete declaration requirement. FHIR-I minutes for 2018-10-08 confirm the persuasive vote and rationale, and a later Zulip thread confirms acceptUnknown was intentionally removed because a single boolean did not fit real implementations.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scope source already reflects the approved correction and no necessary source hunk remains for FHIR-18363.
